text: Build the answer bit by bit; O(log n).

Walking down a Fenwick tree (树状数组倒着走 / 树状数组上二分): to find the smallest position p with prefix sum ≥ k, do not binary search with O(log n) queries each (O(log² n)). Instead build p bit by bit from the top: for step = 2⌊log n⌋ down to 1, if p + step ≤ n and t[p + step] < k, move p += step and k −= t[p].
The answer is p + 1. O(log n).

It works because t[p + step] covers exactly (p, p + step] when p is a multiple of 2·step, which holds at every stage of the walk. With a Fenwick tree of value counts this is "k-th smallest in a multiset" in O(log n), the job usually given to a balanced tree.

Deletions are add(x, −1). Values must be in 1 … V (discretise first). The same walk finds "first position where the prefix sum exceeds S" for any non-negative array.
Subtree = [tin, tout]; four operations.

DFS order (DFS 序): number vertices by entry time tin[u] and record tout[u] = the last entry time inside u's subtree. Then the subtree of u is exactly the range [tin[u], tout[u]], so subtree operations become range operations on an array (Fenwick or segment tree).

Combinations with two Fenwick trees: subtree add + single-vertex query (range add, point query); vertex add + subtree sum (point add, range sum); subtree add + subtree sum (range add, range sum, 拓展篇第26章). Path-to-root sums: add v at tin[u] and −v at tout[u] + 1, then a point query at tin[x] sums the values of x's ancestors (Promotion Counting P3605 uses DFS order with a Fenwick tree over values).

A persistent 0-1 trie (可持久化 Trie): version i = the trie of a1 … ai, built from version i − 1 by copying one root-to-leaf path (like a persistent segment tree, 进阶篇第8章), with a count in every node. Counts of version r minus version l − 1 describe exactly al … ar.

Maximum of x ⊕ ai over i ∈ [l, r]: walk both versions from the top bit, prefer the opposite bit of x whenever the count difference there is positive. With prefix XORs it answers "maximum XOR of a suffix ending in a range" (最大异或和 P4735).

Keep the newest vector at each bit.

A prefix linear basis (前缀线性基) answers "maximum xor of a subset of a[l..r]" online. Keep, for every prefix r, a basis where each vector remembers the largest position it comes from. When inserting ar with position r, at each bit where the stored vector is older, swap them (the newer one stays, the older one continues down).

Then the basis of prefix r restricted to vectors with position ≥ l spans exactly the xors of a[l..r]. Query: greedy from the high bit, using only vectors with pos ≥ l. O(log V) per insert and query (CF1100F Ivan and Burgers).

One walk down the tree; O(log n).

Binary search on a segment tree (线段树上二分): to find the first index i ≥ l with ai ≥ x, do not binary search outside with O(log n) queries each (O(log² n)). Walk the tree once: skip any node outside [l, n] or with max < x; otherwise go left first, then right. O(log n), because only O(log n) nodes are partly inside and each full node is entered only if its answer is there.
The same walk finds the k-th one (descend by counts), the first prefix with sum ≥ s (descend by sums, 第 1 节 is the Fenwick version), and the last index ≤ r satisfying a condition (go right first).
